statement: The word TIGER is written again and again with no gaps: TIGERTIGERTIGER and so on. What is the 18th letter?

choices.misconception: I found that letter 15 ends a word and gave the first letter of the next word, which is letter 16.
I counted one letter too few and gave the 17th letter.
I counted one letter too many and gave the 19th letter.
I found that the third TIGER ends at letter 15 and gave that letter instead of counting on.

hints: Each TIGER uses the same number of letters.
The pattern repeats every 5 letters. Jump ahead a whole word at a time until you are close to 18, then count the last few letters one by one.
Three whole words use 15 letters, so letter 15 is an R. Count on 3 more letters from the start of the next TIGER.

solutions.reliable: TIGER has 5 letters, so the words end at letters 5, 10 and 15. Letter 16 is T, letter 17 is I and letter 18 is G. The idea to keep: in a repeating pattern, jump by whole repeats, then count only the leftover steps.
solutions.elegant: Counting in fives, 18 is 3 more than 15, so the 18th letter is the 3rd letter of TIGER, which is G. The idea to keep: the leftover after the last full repeat tells you the position in the pattern.

whyOnTest: Finding a far-away place in a repeating pattern rewards jumping by whole repeats instead of counting every letter.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
